speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned suffering from a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to begin our assessment, how long has this cough persisted, and have you noticed any specific triggers, such as exposure to cold air or smoke?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

The duration of symptoms (11 years), the description of "copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum," and the failure of recurrent antibiotic treatments to cure the underlying condition strongly suggest bronchiectasis rather than simple chronic bronchitis. I am requesting a High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the chest to visualize the characteristic bronchial dilation and confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CTA (High Resolution)
